patterns.title: Integer transformation diverges between allocation and memory access
patterns.invariant: Every attacker-influenced value used to size storage must remain in the same validated numeric domain as the independent value that controls the later read, write, copy, or loop bound.
investigation_steps: Trace the original signedness and width through each cast and arithmetic operation.
Write separate symbolic expressions for allocated bytes and maximum accessed bytes.
Check negative, zero, maximum, wraparound, and narrowing boundaries before the first memory access.
required_evidence: A source-to-transform-to-allocation-to-access trace using actual C types.
The missing or insufficient numeric guard and a reachable boundary value.
falsifiers: A dominating checked arithmetic operation rejects every overflowing or negative value.
Allocation and access are proven to use the same validated expression and unit.

patterns.title: Capacity contract is lost across calls, aliases, or consumed-length returns
patterns.invariant: At every call boundary, remaining capacity must be expressed in the callee's unit and must cover all writes and pointer advances, including bytes reported as consumed or required.
investigation_steps: Normalize element counts, byte counts, offsets, and return values to one unit.
Follow pointer aliases and remaining-capacity updates through callers and callees.
Compare success, retry, truncation, and failure paths for asymmetric state updates.
required_evidence: A caller-to-callee capacity equation with every unit and state mutation identified.
A path where required output or pointer movement can exceed the proved remainder.
falsifiers: A dominating guard covers total consumption in a common unit on every return path.
The callee cannot write or advance beyond the capacity explicitly passed by the caller.

patterns.title: Formatted representation can exceed a fixed destination
patterns.invariant: The maximum formatted representation, including sign, prefix, precision, exponent, separators, and terminator, must fit the actual remaining destination capacity.
investigation_steps: Identify fixed or caller-provided destination capacity and the format-controlled maximum expansion.
Trace precision, width, locale, numeric magnitude, and custom formatter callbacks.
Verify the bounded API result is checked before the destination is consumed.
required_evidence: The destination capacity and a source-backed upper bound for formatted output.
A reachable input or configuration that violates the bound.
falsifiers: A checked size-query or bounded formatter proves and enforces sufficient capacity.
The input domain has a source-backed maximum representation smaller than the buffer.

patterns.title: Parser cursor mutation invalidates a prior length check
patterns.invariant: The dominating remaining-input check must cover the largest post-mutation dereference index after every cursor advance and across every parser call boundary.
investigation_steps: Record the remaining-length relation before the guard, after each mutation, and at callee entry.
Compute the maximum dereference index for each tag, extension, or variable-length branch.
Exercise minimum remaining input and maximum accepted length boundaries.
required_evidence: An exact guard-to-advance-to-read relation with numeric indices.
Caller and callee evidence when mutation and dereference occur in different functions.
falsifiers: A post-mutation dominating guard covers the maximum dereference index.
The reader is unreachable unless the caller proves the required remaining length.

patterns.title: Signed parser value reaches an index before domain validation
patterns.invariant: A parsed or computed index must be proven non-negative and strictly below the destination extent after its final conversion and before any array access.
investigation_steps: Trace lexer, parser, enum, sentinel, and arithmetic values into the final index type.
Check negative, sentinel, truncated, and maximum values on recovery and normal paths.
Verify both lower and upper bounds dominate every read and write.
required_evidence: The value domain at parse time and after the final C conversion.
A reachable access missing either the lower or upper bound.
falsifiers: Both bounds are checked after the final conversion and dominate the access.
The type and construction make negative or oversized values unrepresentable.

patterns.title: Encoding expansion and retry paths disagree about output capacity
patterns.invariant: Before consuming input or partially writing an encoded unit, remaining output capacity must cover the unit's maximum expansion and retry must preserve identical cursor and capacity state.
investigation_steps: Enumerate minimum and maximum bytes emitted per input unit and normalization mode.
Compare preflight, partial-write, flush, retry, and error-state mutations.
Verify the retry begins from a consistent input cursor and output remainder.
required_evidence: A per-unit expansion bound and output-state equation across retry.
A boundary where partial progress violates that equation.
falsifiers: Capacity is checked for maximum expansion before any state mutation.
Retry restores or preserves every input and output state variable atomically.

patterns.title: Reallocation failure violates ownership of the original buffer
patterns.invariant: A failed reallocation must leave exactly one well-defined owner of the original allocation, and every caller must observe the same pointer and ownership state.
investigation_steps: Distinguish temporary-result and in-place reallocation idioms.
Trace aliases and cleanup labels on every allocation-failure return.
Inject allocator failure at each growth site and observe final ownership.
required_evidence: The ownership state before and after the failed allocation.
A reachable double free, stale use, or unrecoverable leak on cleanup.
falsifiers: The original pointer remains owned and is released exactly once by a documented caller.
Ownership is transferred atomically only after successful allocation.

patterns.title: Output or callback failure bypasses resource cleanup
patterns.invariant: Every resource acquired before an external write, callback, or serialization step must have one cleanup path for every success and failure result.
investigation_steps: List acquired resources and enumerate all returns after each fallible operation.
Compare direct returns, cleanup labels, callback ownership, and partial output paths.
Force the first and last failure after allocation to verify cleanup symmetry.
required_evidence: A concrete acquire-to-failure path that skips or duplicates cleanup.
The repeated or attacker-triggerable impact of the resource imbalance.
falsifiers: A single dominating cleanup path releases each resource exactly once.
The callee contract proves ownership transfer before the failing operation.
